items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I was working with Thelonius, we had another job... We was working opposite Blood, Sweat and Tears... Philly Joe Jeffrey Jones on drums, Paul Jeffries on tenor and myself.

ctx.x: He had went up to the Zildjian cymbal house and got a whole lot of cymbals and a great big gong. So he had it in his head when the announcer announced Thelonius, "Thelonius Monk," you know, come on the stand, we would step out on the bandstand. Beaver sit down and I take my (inaudible) the bass and Beaver would draw back with this mallet. He's going to hit the gong and he missed the whole gong. Very embarrassing, but you know, people in the club was very stiff. They was, you know, but Monk was very angry by…
So, when we got back -- well, I mean. I want to tell you something else. I hadn't seen Erroll Garner in years

ctx.x: And Monk called me up just to play on one track of his Thelonious's album, his solo album. And about this time, Johnnie Griffin was in New York; Jimmy Mann was there working, and Wilbur Camel came out from Chicago, so Keepnews people said, 'well, it's time for your own ...' he didn't call me until Lionel phoned me; he got word to me, and he say, 'You got a date tomorrow', and I said, 'My date? I got no material.' And he said, 'Well, you be in the studio at such and such a time.'
Thelonious Himself Johnny Junior Mance Campbell
Wilbur, 'cause I didn't have a phone
